articles.author: Etelka Lehoczky
articles.description: Dillard's work was characterized by spare prose and a deep connection to nature. She is best known for Pilgrim at Tinker Creek, An American Childhood, The Maytrees and The Writing Life.

articles.author: Krishani Dhanji
articles.description:
Follow the day’s news live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Barnaby Joyce says Labor is copying and pasting One Nation’s homework because the measures we know so far around blocking the families of international students and preventing visa hopping have some similarity to what Pauline Hanson is suggesting.
Speaking to the Today show a little earlier, Joyce says Burke’s last minute cancellation at the press club was “the greatest no-show since Amelia Earhart”.
[Burke] can’t possibly be about to announce One Nation’s policy. I mean, Tony’s a great guy, right? I like Tony, but honestly, he was the greatest no-show since Amelia Earhart when he didn’t turn up to the Press Club …
What I’ve heard thus far is that it’s an exact replication, but not to the extent of what One Nation is doing.
I will be watching this with absolute fascination and some trepidation, and I’ll be waiting for Jim Chalmers to explain his new budget.
I was on polling booths with my colleagues like Sally Sitou. I was out there in Reid with her in those last weeks of the campaign, standing there for hours at a time. She would be surrounded by men a foot taller than her, stopping her physically talking to or giving information to voters.
I would think secretly paying known rightwing figures to disrupt events and pretend that they are just disgruntled citizens having their say is certainly immoral, if it’s not illegal.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australian politics live: Burke hoses down accusations of tension with Albanese and Chalmers, saying he was ‘surprised’ by reports

articles.author: Patrick Greenfield. Photographs by Scott Creel
articles.description:
As three siblings came of age and had to leave their pack, scientists tracked the dogs’ perilous 2,500-mile odyssey to find their own territory
It sounds like a Disney movie: three wild dogs, all brothers, on an epic journey to find a home of their own after their family tells them to leave. They dodge cars and hunters in search of a new life, navigating bushmeat snares and the hostility of a human-dominated landscape until they find a new haven on the African savannah.
But this is exactly what happened in Zambia last year, when three endangered African wild dogs made the longest-ever recorded single journey of any mammal from the continent. The brothers travelled more than 2,500 miles (4,100km) over eight months in their “dispersal” – when a young dog comes of age and must establish new territory to find a mate and start a family of their own.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Like a Disney movie’: Three wild dog brothers make Africa’s longest journey

articles.author: Steven Morris
articles.description:
Initiative aims to keep alive age-old skill, and at Muchelney Abbey in Somerset improve habitat for rare shrill carder bee
It sounds like something out of a Thomas Hardy novel: a merry band of men and women roaming the West Country cutting meadows by hand in exchange for hunks of bread and cheese.
But the conservation charity English Heritage is recruiting a team of volunteer scythers to maintain 21st-century meadowland in the old-fashioned way.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: English Heritage trains new generation of scythers to maintain meadows and craft

articles.author: Ruth Michaelson in Istanbul
articles.description:
Protesters teargassed as minister claims widespread raids and arrests under obscenity laws were to ‘protect families’ 
Turkish authorities have used accusations of obscenity to justify a wave of raids and arrests targeting the LGBTQ+ community, which has grown to include journalists as well as more than 150 arrested during protests against the raids.
Starting in the early hours of Sunday, Turkish police carried out simultaneous raids on the offices of LGBTQ+ rights organisations and HIV-advocacy groups in the cities of Istanbul, the capital, Ankara, and the coastal city of İzmir, as well as the cities of Aydın and Mersin.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Turkey detains dozens in crackdown on LGBTQ+ activists and journalists

articles.author: Amanda Meade
articles.description:
Former 2GB and 2UE broadcaster has pleaded not guilty to 22 indecent assault and sexual touching charges

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

An alleged victim of Alan Jones has told a Sydney court that an unwanted kiss from the former shock jock more than a decade ago is seared in his memory and he wished it never happened.
The ex-sportsman, known as complainant M, agreed during cross-examination by the defence that he sent Jones a shirtless photo of him in Paris some months before the alleged kiss.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Prominent athlete tells Alan Jones trial he sent shirtless photo before unwanted kiss he wished ‘never happened’

articles.author: Robert Mackey, Shrai Popat, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Sign up for the US Breaking News email

US Federal Reserve raises interest rates for the first time since 2023

Reader Q&A: how united are the Democrats ahead of the US midterms?

Later today, my colleagues and I will be hosting a live Q&A all about how united the Democratic party is ahead of the November midterms.
We’ll be digging into who are the Democrats running in the upcoming election and where they stand. 
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump blasts interest rate uptick and claims ‘hostile’ Federal Reserve board made decision ‘only for political reasons’ – as it happened

articles.author: David Smith in Gastonia, North Carolina and Lauren Gambino
articles.description:
President stumps for Senate nominee Michael Whatley in North Carolina and urges voters to ‘crush the communists’
Donald Trump returned to the campaign trail on Wednesday, imploring North Carolina voters to “pretend I’m on the ticket” and “crush the communists” in the November elections at a rally in support of the Republican Senate nominee Michael Whatley.
Despite Trump’s deep unpopularity, Republicans hope to once again turn the president’s loyal following into a political force as the party confronts an unforgiving midterm landscape.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Pretend I’m on the ticket’: Trump hits campaign trail in bid to boost Republican hopes

articles.author: Kate Lamb
articles.description:
Government estimates that one in 60 adults in Fiji now living with HIV, as escalating use of methamphetamine fuels ‘epidemic’
Fiji has declared a national HIV emergency amid a spike in infections as the Pacific nation grapples with a correlating rise in methamphetamine use.
The country’s health and medical services minister, Dr Ratu Atonio Lalabalavu, said in a statement on social media that an outbreak-level response was no longer sufficient to address what he described an “epidemic”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fiji declares national HIV emergency as Pacific nation grapples with surge in cases

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
The US president call the move a ‘hostile act’, as Canada seeks to move closer to the EU and diversify its defence ties
Donald Trump has threatened the European Union with “serious tariffs” and a cut to trade after the bloc proposed to make Canada its first ever associate member, calling the idea “laughable”.
Suggesting the move was a “hostile act”, the US president told reporters he could put “very serious tariffs or stop trading with Europe”. He added: “If it’s a good intention, that’s fine. If it’s a bad intention, we’ll put very heavy tariffs on Europe.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump calls EU offer to Canada of associate membership ‘laughable’, while threatening tariffs

articles.author: Krishani Dhanji and Tom McIlroy
articles.description:
Independent senator had denounced as ‘cruel’ the plan to impose a $5,000 cap on allied health services for veterans

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Labor has backed down on plans to impose a $5,000 cap on health services for defence veterans, caving to growing political pressure after weeks of criticism.
The government announced it would no longer pursue the cap for allied health services, which had been to come into force on 1 July 2027, after a weeks-long campaign by the opposition, veterans’ groups and independent senator Jacqui Lambie.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘The bloody cap has been scrapped’: Jacqui Lambie celebrates Labor backdown on veterans’ health services cap

articles.author: Nick Visser
articles.description:
Boys aged 14 and 16 charged after Marco Tapia, 23, was killed inside his family’s home in Glen Alpine

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Two teenage boys have been charged with murder after the shooting death of a university student in Sydney this month, which police say was a case of mistaken identity.
Marco Tapia, 23, was shot inside his family’s home in Glen Alpine early on 1 September.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Teenage boys charged with murder after alleged mistaken identity shooting of Sydney student

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
The US artist, whose swirly, colorful, instantly recognizable designs became hugely commercially successful, died on Monday
Peter Max, whose colorful, psychedelic pop art expressed the optimism of the “flower power” movement of the 1960s and graced everything from postage stamps to a cruise ship, has died at 88.
Max died on Monday, his son, Adam Max, said in a written statement on Wednesday. No cause was given.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Peter Max, psychedelic pop artist who epitomized flower power, dies aged 88

articles.author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
articles.description:
Warning comes as forecast for nation’s economic growth downgraded amid concerns over rising debt and inflation

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The International Monetary Fund has called on Australia’s federal and state governments to cut spending as it warns the Reserve Bank may have to hike interest rates further to get price pressures back under control.
More disciplined budgets would rein in rising debt burdens and help solve Australia’s long-running inflation problem, the IMF said in a new report, as it downgraded its forecast for Australia’s economic growth in 2027.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: IMF urges Australian government to cut spending as another interest rate hike looms

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
LeJames Norman, 40, killed at Huntsville penitentiary while scheduled execution in Georgia halted by judge
A man convicted over the shooting deaths of three people was executed on Wednesday in Texas, while another execution scheduled for the same time in Georgia was halted by a judge.
It’s the fifth execution in Texas this year. Georgia has yet to put anyone to death this year. The nation’s busiest death chamber is in Florida, which accounted for more than half the 25 executions already carried out in the US this year.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Texas kills man by lethal injection in state’s fifth execution this year

articles.author: Cecilia Nowell
articles.description:
Pair accused of misappropriating millions in taxpayer dollars as Trump officials target alleged fraud in blue states
Federal law enforcement officers have arrested two employees of California-based homelessness non-profits on corruption charges, alleging that they misappropriated millions in taxpayer dollars.
The US justice department has arrested Michael Young, a founder of the Culver City-based nonprofit Home At Last, and Lakiya Malone, an employee of the Los Angeles-based Special Service for Groups. The two are expected to appear in court on Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: LA homelessness non-profit workers arrested over alleged corruption and bribes

articles.author: Damien Gayle
articles.description:
Scientists say global heating was a destabilising factor in collapse of 200,000 sq metre glacier in August
Climate breakdown probably weakened the glacier that collapsed causing catastrophic floods and killing hundreds of people in Nepal and Tibet last month, the first scientific study of the disaster has found.
Researchers identified unusually warm conditions before the glacier’s collapse, which sent an avalanche of 110m cubic metres (3,885 cu ft) of snow and ice into the valley below. This triggered flash floods on an almost unprecedented scale, hitting communities downstream without warning.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Climate crisis likely behind devastating Nepal-Tibet floods that killed more than 1,300, first study finds

articles.author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
articles.description:
Pro-Israel Gregory Meeks raises concerns over threat to civilian lives from package of 40,000 one-ton bombs

‘An antidote to Trumpism’: Our politics team answered your questions on Democrats’ midterms hopes

The top Democrat on the House foreign affairs committee has thrown up a roadblock to one of the largest US arms transfers of Trump’s second term, refusing to clear a $2.8bn sale of 2,000lb bombs to Israel.
Gregory Meeks announced the hold on Tuesday on a package of 40,000 of the bombs, among the most destructive conventional munitions in the US arsenal.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Key House Democrat refuses to clear Trump’s $2.8bn arms sale to Israel

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll and Jessica Elgot
articles.description:
Government sources say legislation aimed at China poses a risk to British businesses and must be addressed
The UK government’s EU reset summit will be delayed again unless the bloc agrees to discuss legislation that could lock British business out of parts of EU industry, government sources have said.
The “Made in Europe” legislation – formally known as the Industrial Accelerator Act – is designed to curb China’s increasing presence in European industry, but was not on the reset plan agreed by the former prime minister Keir Starmer and the European Commission chief, Ursula von der Leyen, in London in May 2025.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Made in Europe’ law threatens UK plans for reset with EU

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
articles.description:
Ursula von der Leyen has opened door for Canada to become associate member to deepen links in ‘openly hostile world’
Canada’s prime minister, Mark Carney, has been advocating closer alignment with “middle powers” since January in the face of recklessness in Washington.
But what should worry another middle power, the UK, is that it was Brussels that came up with Wednesday’s big reveal in Strasbourg.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is EU’s offer to Canada a blueprint for Britain – or a reminder it is out in the cold?

articles.author: Robyn Vinter and agency
articles.description:
Ivan Jennings, 46, sentenced to five years after pleading guilty to encouraging terrorism on social media
A rightwing extremist who discussed poisoning Jews and Muslims and called for the killing of migrants and minority communities has been jailed.
Ivan Jennings, 46, called for the murder of hundreds of people he labelled “subhumans”, saying it was “justified and actually needed”, in extreme far-right groups over a period of three months in 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: English far-right extremist who discussed killing Jews, Muslims and migrants is jailed

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
articles.description:
Mark Rutte asks UK and Europe to ‘provide hard power Nato needs’ in face of geopolitical uncertainty
Nato needs “more UK and more Europe” to deal with the most dangerous security environment faced by the west in a generation, the secretary general of the 32-country military alliance said this afternoon on a visit to the UK.
Mark Rutte praised Britain for promising to increase defence spending in line with US demands after a meeting prime minister Andy Burnham – but argued that the military and financial effort must continue into the future.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nato leader warns of ‘most dangerous and complex security environment in a generation’

articles.author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Ten category C prisons in England and Wales asked to add second beds, in breach of safe occupancy limits
The Prison Service has drawn up plans to “double up” hundreds of prisoners in temporary prefabricated cells built for one person, at the request of the Ministry of Justice, leaked documents show.
Amid an ongoing overcrowding crisis in England and Wales, governors of 10 category C prisons have been asked to sign off the installation of second beds in “rapid deployment cells [RDCs]”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Prisoners to ‘double up’ in one-person prefab cells, leaked documents show

articles.author: Patrick Greenfield
articles.description:
MSPs vote for strict environmental impact assessments and will delay decisions until national strategy is developed
Holyrood has voted to pause planning applications for all new AI datacentres for up to a year until the Scottish government has developed a national strategy.
On Wednesday, MSPs backed a Scottish Labour motion to halt new schemes for up to 12 months while rules on hyperscale datacentres are developed in what could be a blow to the British government’s AI strategy.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Planning permission for new Scottish AI datacentres suspended for up to a year

articles.author: Chris Stein
articles.description:
Three more GOP members voted for war powers resolution to force withdrawal from the conflict as election looms

US politics live – latest updates

As the US war with Iran drags on, the ranks of Republicans signaling the conflict is a liability for their party continues to grow.
When the House of Representatives on Tuesday evening considered its sixth war powers resolution intended to force Donald Trump to withdraw troops from the conflict, three Republicans who had not supported the previous efforts broke with their party to vote this one to passage. Earlier that day, a Republican who had lost his primary after repeatedly clashing with Trump proposed impeaching the US defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, alleging a variety of constitutional transgressions including prosecuting the war against Iran without congressional authorization.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: More Republicans are turning on Iran war as midterms come into view

articles.author: Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem, Seham Tantesh in Gaza and agencies
articles.description:
Rescue workers say search for dozens of people hampered by lack of heavy machinery
A building housing about 100 displaced Palestinian families has collapsed in Gaza City, killing at least 21 people in their sleep, including 11 children, forcing rescuers to dig through the rubble with their bare hands as they search for dozens of people believed to be trapped.
A rescue team from Gaza’s civil defence said they had recovered the bodies of five children among the victims, while 25 injured people were taken to hospital. Medical sources said rescuers could hear the voices of people trapped beneath the rubble as they tried to reach them.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: At least 21 killed after Israeli-hit building in Gaza City collapses

articles.author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
articles.description:
Rachida Dati accused of lobbying for carmaker Renault-Nissan when she was member of European parliament
Rachida Dati, a former French culture minister, has gone on trial in Paris on corruption charges linked to dealings with the Renault-Nissan carmaking group.
Dati, 60, is accused of illegal lobbying when she accepted €900,000 (£770,000) in lawyer’s fees from a Netherlands-based subsidiary of Renault-Nissan while she was a member of the European parliament. The court will have to decide what the money was for.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Former French culture minister goes on trial over corruption charges

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
articles.description:
String of female murder victims found near Johannesburg’s international airport, including five in the past week
The discovery of the bodies of eight women around Johannesburg’s international airport, including five in the past week, has prompted an outpouring of fear, grief and anger over a lack of progress in tackling femicide.
When Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo did not return after going for a run on 9 September, her eight-year-old daughter alerted relatives, who contacted police. The 38-year-old’s body was found on Saturday and identified by relatives on Monday. The news of her disappearance had gone viral.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We are prey’: discovery of seven women’s bodies fuels anger over femicide in South Africa

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Iran-backed militants have offered Trump administration assurances over safety of Red Sea shipping
Officials from the US met Houthi leaders over the weekend at the country’s embassy in Muscat, Oman, it has been confirmed, leading to the US decision not to intervene to help Saudi Arabia drive back a Houthi advance inside Yemen.
The Iran-backed militant group reassured the US that the ceasefire agreement between the two sides struck in 2025 still held and the movement had no intention of attacking US shipping in the Red Sea. Only Saudi-linked shipping was regarded as a target owing to its blockade of Yemen, the Houthis confirmed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US opts not to back Saudi Arabia in Yemen after meeting Houthi leaders

articles.author: Andrew Pulver
articles.description:
Passionate documentary maker  won international acclaim for unsparing but poetic films exploring the impact of the Pinochet regime in Chile 
Patricio Guzmán, the film-maker who chronicled Chile’s bloody 1970s political strife and its subsequent social and political turmoil in films such as The Battle of Chile and Nostalgia for the Light, has died aged 85. According to Chilean news outlet Emol, Guzmán died on Tuesday in Paris after a cardiorespiratory arrest.
Guzmán’s chief preoccupation throughout his career was the carnage unleashed by Augusto Pinochet’s coup in 1973 against Salvador Allende, Chile’s elected president. He later told the Guardian: “I’m a film-maker who was very marked by the ways of the dictator. It has remained with me for ever. I cannot leave it behind.” However, he resisted the idea that he was an activist, political film-maker, adding: “I’m not a sociologist. Neither am I a politician. I make films that are metaphorical and poetic; I interpret reality through my own personal way of looking.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Battle of Chile director Patricio Guzmán dies aged 85

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
articles.description:
Announcement of visa restrictions follows Trump’s false claims of ‘white genocide’ taking place in South Africa
The US has announced visa restrictions on some South Africans as Donald Trump’s administration continues to claim that South Africa’s government racially discriminates against white minority Afrikaners.
The announcement did not specify individuals who were barred from the US. Trump has spent his second term falsely claiming there is a “white genocide” in South Africa and railing against its affirmative action policies.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US to bar some South Africans over claims of anti-white discrimination

articles.author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
articles.description:
Prosecutors sought jail term for chief executive of Evett after insects not approved for consumption were on menu
A South Korean court has fined the operator of one of Seoul’s most celebrated restaurants and its chief executive for serving a dessert topped with ants, an insect not approved for consumption under local food safety law.
The operator of Evett, a two-Michelin-star restaurant in the affluent Gangnam district, was fined 10m won (£5,400) and its chief executive 15m won, Newsis reported.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Michelin-starred Seoul restaurant fined for serving dessert topped with ants

articles.author: Deepa Parent
articles.description:
Leaked documents and testimony reveal extent of regime’s crackdown in 2022 and how it paved the way for more brutal killings of protesters this year
Iranian security forces “coordinated” the killing, torture and sexual abuse of hundreds of people who took part in the women-led nationwide protests in September 2022, according to leaked state documents and interviews.
Tens of thousands of people, including children, took to the streets of towns and cities across Iran after the death in custody of Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old Kurdish woman, after her arrest by the “morality” police for allegedly not complying with the country’s hijab regulations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Iranian security forces coordinated killing, torture and sexual abuse of protesters, says Amnesty

articles.author: Jason Burke International security correspondent
articles.description:
Twenty-five years after 9/11, figures compiled by conflict monitor underline how Sahel region has become centre of Islamist terror
Islamist extremist violence in Africa’s Sahel region is set to reach historic highs after a series of sweeping offensives by groups linked to al-Qaida and Islamic State, according to new figures compiled by the conflict monitor Acled.
As the US marks the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks launched by al-Qaida against targets in Washington and New York, the statistics underline the continued expansion of the veteran organisation in parts of Africa – in stark contrast with its relative weakness elsewhere.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Al-Qaida and IS-linked violence in Africa’s Sahel belt set to hit record levels this year

articles.author: David Conn Investigations correspondent
articles.description:
Dozens of Bank of England directors and founding subscribers invested in trafficking of enslaved Africans
The Bank of England and the British financial system were for centuries deeply involved in the enslavement and transatlantic trafficking of millions of African people, according to new research on Britain’s slavery history.
Research by historians compiling the Register of British Slave Traders has found that the scale of the financial system’s involvement in enslavement is greater than previously known or acknowledged. The Bank of England, the central bank owned by the government since nationalisation by Clement Attlee’s Labour administration in 1946, had dozens of financiers involved in its foundation who were also significant investors in the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds

articles.author: Jonathan Watts
articles.description:
Defenders of forests and rivers killed at rate of one every three days in 2025, with 85% of deaths in Latin America
Nature and land defenders were murdered at the rate of one every three days last year, prompting many communities to set up self-defence units, according to the latest annual death toll by the independent watchdog Global Witness.
Organised crime groups or professional killers were implicated in more than a third of the 124 killings of defenders in 2025 as narco-trafficking activities overlapped with intrusions into indigenous territories and environmental crime, such as illegal logging and wildcat gold mining.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: People protecting nature and land set up self-defence units amid threat of murder

articles.author: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
Scandal explodes as country’s election campaign peaks, with polls suggesting dead heat between candidates
Brazil’s supreme court has been thrust into what experts consider the greatest crisis since the return of democracy in the 1980s, as two rival judges lock horns on the eve of the presidential election with unpredictable consequences for Latin America’s largest democracy.
The politically charged dispute exploded into public view on Tuesday as judges traded insults and accusations during a heated supreme court hearing that was livestreamed into millions of Brazilian homes.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ferocious fight among Brazil’s supreme court erupts on eve of presidential election

articles.author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto and Jennifer Rankin in Strasbourg
articles.description:
Prime minister speaks of strengthening Canada’s economic and political ties to Europe at Canada Investment Summit
Mark Carney said Canada will pursue a “unique security and economic alliance” with Europe as he positions his country as a base to build in the “new global economic order”.
Speaking to investors, company executives and government ministers at the inaugural Canada Investment Summit on Tuesday, the prime minister pitched Canada as a “safe harbour” and lucrative home for foreign capital as his government looks to reduce its reliance on trade with the United States.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Carney says Canada will pursue ‘unique security and economic alliance’ with EU amid US trade spat

articles.author: Gloria Dickie
articles.description:
Critically endangered Bornean orangutans flee forests as staff at Rangkong research station work round the clock to stave off blaze
Wildfires in Indonesia are sweeping through a critical research site for Bornean orangutans and are now threatening a celebrated research camp, home to one of the world’s longest-running studies of wild apes.
In the past few days, the fires have burned within 200 metres of Rangkong research station, a satellite of Cabang Panti research station, which lies about four miles north in Gunung Palung national park.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Indonesian wildfires threaten leading orangutan research site in Borneo

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi and Shah Meer Baloch in Islamabad
articles.description:
Kasim and Sulaiman Khan tell Guardian they believe ex-PM is being ‘slowly killed’ by harsh treatment, driven by Asim Munir
The sons of Imran Khan have accused Pakistan’s powerful army chief of a “personal vendetta” against the incarcerated former prime minister and expressed fears their father is being “slowly killed” in jail, as international pressure mounts over his prison conditions.
Kasim Khan, 27, and Sulaiman Khan, 29, have become strong advocates for the release of their father, who has been held in Adiala prison in Rawalpindi since his arrest in 2023, and is serving a 14-year sentence on corruption charges.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Imran Khan’s sons accuse Pakistani army chief of vendetta against imprisoned father

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
After a five-storey building collapsed in Delhi, focus is on how urban areas can adapt to growing populations. Plus, Ahmedabad’s ace newspaper delivery driver goes viral
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
Recently, I may have saved a woman’s life on the road. Somehow, this was something I had expected to happen.
On that day, I saw a truck leave a construction site with a tangled wire trailing behind. I frantically looked to see what the wire was attached to and spotted the scaffolding a few meters ahead. I shrieked and grabbed the hand of the woman walking in front of me just as the metal pipes came crashing down. We hugged for a brief second, and then walked our separate ways.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What would it take to make India’s cities better – and safer?

articles.author: Mark Saunokonoko with Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Planned daily reductions will further choke one of the world’s most important shipping lanes
The Panama canal plans to again cut maritime traffic due to worsening drought caused by the El Niño climate phenomenon, further choking up one of the world’s most important shipping lanes.
The canal handles 5% of global maritime trade and about 40% of US container traffic; it is favoured by shippers because it usually reduces cost and transit times, especially for companies trading between China, Asia and the US.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Panama canal traffic facing further cuts as drought from El Niño worsens

articles.author: Lauren Almeida
articles.description:
Donald Trump dismisses attempts to increase controls on artificial intelligence as ‘sick conspiracy’  
AI-linked stocks tumbled on Monday after the bosses of Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX called for a slowdown in AI “reckless” development, citing fears the technology could soon run out of control.
Shares in the semiconductor designer Nvidia – the world’s most valuable company – were down 3.3% by market closing in New York City, while Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) slid 4% and Micron Technology and Sandisk shares slumped by 5%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq index fund was down 0.5% by the end of the day.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: AI-linked stocks slide after tech bosses call for slowdown in ‘reckless’ development

articles.author: Caitlin Cassidy
articles.description:
Police in Bali believe the two young children died as a result of violence, while a 57-year-old man is believed to have taken his own life 
Indonesian police are investigating the deaths of three Australians who died in Bali over the weekend, with initial reports suggesting a father killed his two young children before taking his own life.
The man, 57, and his two children, seven and four, who are also Indonesian citizens, were discovered deceased in a bungalow in Kuta on Sunday morning.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Indonesian police investigate deaths of Australian man and two children in Bali as suspected murder-suicide

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
The presidential briefing documents were declassified on the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks
Several dozen presidential briefing documents declassified on Friday, the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, detail intelligence that government officials had gathered about Osama bin Laden and al-Qaida leading up to the hijackings that killed nearly 3,000 people and upended American national security.
The documents illustrate security analysts’ tracking of Bin Laden’s movements and support system, as well as concerns about possible threats to US targets. They also detail officials’ understanding of his network in the United States and other countries, including how his operations were financed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: CIA releases dozens of presidential daily briefs on Bin Laden and al-Qaida from before 9/11

articles.author: Tora Agarwala
articles.description:
Following six years of talks, Pitt Rivers Museum will return body parts collected by British colonial administrators to north-east India
Anthropologists and community leaders from Nagaland, a remote state in north-eastern India bordering Myanmar, have expressed joy and relief that human remains belonging to their ancestors that had been on display in a British museum for nearly a century are finally being returned.
On Monday, the Pitt Rivers Museum in Oxford announced that 39 pieces of human remains – including parts of skulls, a finger and a piece of skin with hair – belonging to the Naga tribes, will be returned to Nagaland after six years of negotiation between the community and the museum.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Our forefathers are coming back’: Naga people celebrate after Oxford museum agrees to return remains

articles.author: Robert Mackey, Shrai Popat, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Sign up for the US Breaking News email

US Federal Reserve raises interest rates for the first time since 2023

Reader Q&A: how united are the Democrats ahead of the US midterms?

Later today, my colleagues and I will be hosting a live Q&A all about how united the Democratic party is ahead of the November midterms.
We’ll be digging into who are the Democrats running in the upcoming election and where they stand. 
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump blasts interest rate uptick and claims ‘hostile’ Federal Reserve board made decision ‘only for political reasons’ – as it happened

articles.author: David Smith in Gastonia, North Carolina and Lauren Gambino
articles.description:
President stumps for Senate nominee Michael Whatley in North Carolina and urges voters to ‘crush the communists’
Donald Trump returned to the campaign trail on Wednesday, imploring North Carolina voters to “pretend I’m on the ticket” and “crush the communists” in the November elections at a rally in support of the Republican Senate nominee Michael Whatley.
Despite Trump’s deep unpopularity, Republicans hope to once again turn the president’s loyal following into a political force as the party confronts an unforgiving midterm landscape.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Pretend I’m on the ticket’: Trump hits campaign trail in bid to boost Republican hopes

articles.author: Cecilia Nowell
articles.description:
Pair accused of misappropriating millions in taxpayer dollars as Trump officials target alleged fraud in blue states
Federal law enforcement officers have arrested two employees of California-based homelessness non-profits on corruption charges, alleging that they misappropriated millions in taxpayer dollars.
The US justice department has arrested Michael Young, a founder of the Culver City-based nonprofit Home At Last, and Lakiya Malone, an employee of the Los Angeles-based Special Service for Groups. The two are expected to appear in court on Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: LA homelessness non-profit workers arrested over alleged corruption and bribes

articles.author: Andrew Roth
articles.description:
Act divides Democrats and Republicans, with some saying it gives president power that could be turned against US allies
The US Congress has passed a sweeping bill allowing Donald Trump to raise tariffs on top buyers of Russian energy and issue other punishing sanctions against the Kremlin following a pitched battle between lawmakers backing Ukraine and sceptics worried the bill gives the president too much power.
The Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 passed in a 262-159 vote on the last day before Congress goes on recess ahead of the midterm elections. Graham, who died earlier this year, co-authored and submitted the bill more than a year and a half ago.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US lawmakers pass bill giving Trump more power to sanction Russia and its enablers

articles.author: Maya Yang
articles.description:
GAO report shows how use paid administrative leave rose by 435% from 2023 to 2025 and incurred a sixfold cost
The US government paid federal workers $9.5bn not to work in 2025 as part of the Trump administration’s attempts to shrink the federal workforce.
As part of efforts by the “department of government efficiency” (Doge), spearheaded by Elon Musk, federal agencies’ use of paid administrative leave rose 435% from 2023 to 2025 – costing six times what the government spent in 2023 – according to a new report released on Tuesday by the Government Accountability Office (GAO), an independent watchdog.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US government paid federal employees $9.5bn not to work amid Doge cuts – report

articles.author: Shakeel Hashim
articles.description:
Trump and Republicans want companies to regulate themselves. It’s a dereliction of duty that will make AI less safe
It is hard to get Sam Altman, Elon Musk and Dario Amodei to agree on much. But over the weekend, all three AI company CEOs called for AI development to slow down in the face of growing, alarming risks. Their employees are sounding the siren too, with one researcher publicly quitting and accusing OpenAI and Anthropic of “gambling with our lives”.
The combination of dire warnings from insiders and growing real-world evidence of rogue AIs should, in a sane world, lead to government action. Instead, Donald Trump and the Republican leadership have their heads in the sand.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The US government is failing Americans on AI | Shakeel Hashim

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
The president’s assistant travelled with him to Ireland – which really shouldn’t be much of a story. But his comms team seems determined to make it one
Passport, money, emotional support human: Donald Trump had all the travel essentials on his recent trip to Ireland. The president flew into Dublin on Saturday morning to play golf, meet the country’s leaders and make provocative comments about unification. Melania didn’t accompany her husband on the trip (“Uh, she sends her regards,” Trump said), but his devoted aide Natalie Harp was obviously at his side.
You’ll know Harp: the 35-year-old assistant was headline news last month after Democratic senator Jon Ossoff quipped that Trump didn’t want to do his job; he just wanted to “build his ballroom and travel with Natalie”. That comment would have been quickly forgotten were it not for the Trump administration’s unhinged response (sample: “Jon Jackoff has to be the biggest cuck loser in politics”), which sparked a media frenzy. There was suddenly a spotlight on Harp, who is nicknamed the “human printer” because she trails the president with a portable printer, ready to hand him hard copies of flattering coverage. She appears to be disturbingly obsessed with her boss and he seems to appreciate the attention: it was recently revealed that Trump gave her (and two other female aides) a cash gift of $45,000 (£33,000) for a nice holiday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why is the White House being so weird about Natalie Harp again? | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: Steven Greenhouse
articles.description:
Not only would the plan do vast economic damage – it assumes that Americans are easily bamboozled
Whenever Donald Trump gives a speech, it’s filled with so many lies and self-serving exaggerations that when he does utter something true, I see that as a sort of marvel. That’s what happened nearly an hour into Trump’s marathon speech last Wednesday at the Republican midterm convention, when he declared: “Only I can make this promise to you.” Trump said that just before he made a promise that was so shameless and irresponsible that what he said was indeed true: only Trump could make such a preposterous promise.
Feeling very generous with other people’s money, the president promised to give $5,000 to every American adult if Republicans retain control of the House and Senate in November. It certainly looked and smelled like a bribe.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s $5,000 pledge to voters is a shameless bribe | Steven Greenhouse

articles.author: Gabrielle Canon
articles.description:
US grapples with federal firefighter shortage as crews say they’re spread thin and lack resources during unrelenting year of fire
Firefighters battling enormous wildfires in the United States say the federal government is failing them at a time when supercharged blazes have made their jobs exponentially more dangerous.
While the US continues to grapple with a critical shortage of federal firefighters – with especially large gaps in essential management positions – the Trump administration has increased pressure on firefighting forces to rapidly and aggressively contain the flames.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We’re near a breaking point:’ firefighters say US government is failing them amid intense wildfire season

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright and Carter Sherman with Johana Bhuiyan . Produced by Tiara Chiaramonte engineered by Ivan Kuraev executive producers Jonathan Menjivar and Rachel Humphreys
articles.description:
A former Anthropic researcher’s apocalyptic declaration about artificial intelligence has led to a global panic that the technology might be the end of us all. At an event in Washington today to warn about the dangers of AI, US senator Bernie Sanders said that Congress has been ‘asleep at the wheel'. Oddly, Steve Bannon appeared at the same event. But is this response a distraction from the more immediate problems AI is already causing? Kai Wright and Carter Sherman are joined by Guardian tech reporter Johana Bhuyian to put this moment in context, and she explains why we should be cynical about industry calls for regulation
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why the real AI apocalypse is already here – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.description:
During a Senate committee hearing, FBI director answered questions from Republican senator John Kennedy about the bureau's new policy allowing the hiring of people who have engaged in bestiality
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kash Patel defends changes in FBI hiring policy regarding bestiality – video

articles.description:
Bernie Sanders criticised the advancement of artificial intelligence at the Pro-Human Assembly in Washington on Tuesday, warning that the current type of AI was 'the least capable version of AI that we will ever have'. The independent senator from Vermont was speaking at the conference alongside a number of AI sceptics, including Steve Bannon
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bernie Sanders says Congress has been ‘asleep at the wheel’ over AI – video

articles.description:
During his 16 August campaign event in Atlanta, Georgia, Senator Jon Ossoff mentioned White House aide Natalie Harp when condemning the Trump administration's handling of the Iran war and USS Lincoln sailors
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jon Ossoff mentions Natalie Harp while condemning Trump's administration – video

articles.author: Francine Prose
articles.description:
A petition against the mayor’s presence reeked of Islamophobia – and ran counter to the sense of togetherness that followed the attacks
Everyone who was in New York on 11 September 2001 has their 9/11 story. My husband and I were at JFK, boarding a plane to San Francisco. Our two sons were home in lower Manhattan, a block away from my 85-year-old mother. They watched the towers fall from our corner. The weather was radiantly beautiful.
For a long time, the faces of the missing were everywhere. Their eyes seemed to follow us from the makeshift shrine outside St Vincent’s hospital to the window of our local bodega. We cried at random moments. We slept badly.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Opposition to Mamdani’s 9/11 remembrance was painful to witness | Francine Prose

articles.author: Sam Levin
articles.description:
Julia Curlee, a former senior CIA officer, speaks on Trump administration’s purge of national security staff, attacks on DEI and failures in Iran war
When the White House fired Julia Curlee from her senior intelligence position in March 2025, her boss had an odd request: please still show up to work on Monday, but be “discreet”.
The longtime CIA analyst had served in Donald Trump’s first term, briefing Vice-President Mike Pence; worked for Joe Biden as a national security director; and stayed on for Trump’s return. She had known her days might be numbered as the incoming White House was ousting national security staffers en masse. Curlee is also transgender, which made her particularly vulnerable as the new administration made anti-trans policies a top priority. But she didn’t understand her boss’s message until she opened her phone and saw the X post:
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The trans CIA official ousted by Trump: ‘We’re a government crippled by its own decisions’

articles.author: Claire Wang
articles.description:
Across the US, anti-datacenter organizers are harnessing community anger to win local elections
After four months of teach-ins and canvassing, Steven Kung helped Monterey Park, just east of Los Angeles, become the first US city to ban datacenter construction. Now, the organizer is running for city council – and he’s taking on an incumbent who supported the development of the sprawling facility.
“The datacenter coming to my neighborhood turned my life upside down,” said Kung. “I saw that there’s a dismantling of democracy at a local level.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: They fought against datacenters. Now they are running for local offices

articles.author: Stephen Starr in Springfield, Ohio
articles.description:
Until Pierre Damas Bel’s death on 31 August, the story of Haitian adolescents in Springfield was one of triumph
At a pavilion west of downtown Springfield, Ohio, 32 high school students dressed in black T-shirts stand silently at a vigil in the warm fall evening air.
Some are holding signs depicting the number 11, as worn on the soccer field by Pierre Damas Bel, the 20-year-old Haitian student and athlete who died in an apparent suicide on 31 August. Other students hold signs that read “live like Pierre” and “Pierre was selfless”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Haitian youths transformed life in an ageing Ohio city. Then Trump made them targets

articles.author: Steven Morris
articles.description:
Initiative aims to keep alive age-old skill, and at Muchelney Abbey in Somerset improve habitat for rare shrill carder bee
It sounds like something out of a Thomas Hardy novel: a merry band of men and women roaming the West Country cutting meadows by hand in exchange for hunks of bread and cheese.
But the conservation charity English Heritage is recruiting a team of volunteer scythers to maintain 21st-century meadowland in the old-fashioned way.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: English Heritage trains new generation of scythers to maintain meadows and craft

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll and Jessica Elgot
articles.description:
Government sources say legislation aimed at China poses a risk to British businesses and must be addressed
The UK government’s EU reset summit will be delayed again unless the bloc agrees to discuss legislation that could lock British business out of parts of EU industry, government sources have said.
The “Made in Europe” legislation – formally known as the Industrial Accelerator Act – is designed to curb China’s increasing presence in European industry, but was not on the reset plan agreed by the former prime minister Keir Starmer and the European Commission chief, Ursula von der Leyen, in London in May 2025.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Made in Europe’ law threatens UK plans for reset with EU

articles.author: Robyn Vinter and agency
articles.description:
Ivan Jennings, 46, sentenced to five years after pleading guilty to encouraging terrorism on social media
A rightwing extremist who discussed poisoning Jews and Muslims and called for the killing of migrants and minority communities has been jailed.
Ivan Jennings, 46, called for the murder of hundreds of people he labelled “subhumans”, saying it was “justified and actually needed”, in extreme far-right groups over a period of three months in 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: English far-right extremist who discussed killing Jews, Muslims and migrants is jailed

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
articles.description:
Mark Rutte asks UK and Europe to ‘provide hard power Nato needs’ in face of geopolitical uncertainty
Nato needs “more UK and more Europe” to deal with the most dangerous security environment faced by the west in a generation, the secretary general of the 32-country military alliance said this afternoon on a visit to the UK.
Mark Rutte praised Britain for promising to increase defence spending in line with US demands after a meeting prime minister Andy Burnham – but argued that the military and financial effort must continue into the future.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nato leader warns of ‘most dangerous and complex security environment in a generation’

articles.author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Ten category C prisons in England and Wales asked to add second beds, in breach of safe occupancy limits
The Prison Service has drawn up plans to “double up” hundreds of prisoners in temporary prefabricated cells built for one person, at the request of the Ministry of Justice, leaked documents show.
Amid an ongoing overcrowding crisis in England and Wales, governors of 10 category C prisons have been asked to sign off the installation of second beds in “rapid deployment cells [RDCs]”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Prisoners to ‘double up’ in one-person prefab cells, leaked documents show

articles.author: Patrick Greenfield
articles.description:
MSPs vote for strict environmental impact assessments and will delay decisions until national strategy is developed
Holyrood has voted to pause planning applications for all new AI datacentres for up to a year until the Scottish government has developed a national strategy.
On Wednesday, MSPs backed a Scottish Labour motion to halt new schemes for up to 12 months while rules on hyperscale datacentres are developed in what could be a blow to the British government’s AI strategy.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Planning permission for new Scottish AI datacentres suspended for up to a year

articles.author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: UK’s Green parties could take 40 seats if result replicated at next election, according to Labour-linked thinktank
The Greens are just four points behind Labour in urban constituencies across the UK, putting them within touching distance of taking as many as 40 seats if the result was replicated at the next election, according to new polling by a Labour-linked thinktank.
The survey by ThinkLabour, which has extensive links to Andy Burnham’s government, finds that urban voters have moved in large numbers towards the UK’s Green parties since the 2024 general election. The research highlights the challenge Labour faces in holding on to the Holborn and St Pancras seat in the face of a challenge from Zack Polanski, the party leader in England and Wales, at next month’s byelection.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Greens just four points behind Labour in urban areas, poll reveals

articles.author: Vikram Dodd Police and crime correspondent
articles.description:
HSBC director Nicholas Brandram, 44, was found unresponsive by emergency services on Tuesday evening 
A senior city banker suspected of pushing a woman into the path of a moving bus in the “Putney pusher” case has been found dead.
Nicholas Brandram, 44, was discovered at his home in Chiswick, west London, on Tuesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Suspect in ‘Putney pusher’ case found dead at his west London home

articles.author: Jamie Grierson
articles.description:
Body found in pond in Suffolk village of Brantham, where Noah was last seen on Tuesday afternoon
Police searching for a three-year-old boy who went missing from a playground on the Suffolk-Essex border have found a body.
Noah Woods was last seen at 3pm on Tuesday in Merriam Close, Brantham, near Manningtree, before becoming separated from a relative.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Body found in search for three-year-old Noah Woods

articles.author: Sally Weale Education correspondent
articles.description:
National Education Union welcomes news that schools will not have to partly fund increase from their own budgets
The UK’s biggest education union is claiming a significant victory after the government bowed to pressure and agreed to fully fund a forthcoming pay increase for teachers in England in a sudden U-turn.
Members of the National Education Union (NEU) were due to vote in a ballot for strike action next month over the government’s recent pay offer which provided for a 3.5% increase from this month, with an additional 3% from next September.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Union claims victory as ministers agree to fully fund pay rise for teachers in England

articles.author: Andrew Sparrow
articles.description:
PM responds to criticism from former Bank of England chief economist
Wes Streeting, the defence secretary, has posted this on social media ahead of Andy Burnham’s meeting with the Nato secretary general Mark Rutte later.
Today I am reminded of the words of my Labour predecessor Denis Healey:
“Once we cut defence expenditure to the extent where our security is imperilled, we have no houses, we have no hospitals, we have no schools. We have a heap of cinders.”
[Britain] is leading, along with Nato allies, the push back against Russia’s dangerous and reckless campaign against us.
Collectively we will continue to strengthen our ability to deter and defend all allies, against any threat. Nato will not be intimidated by Russia’s campaign of hostile actions. Russia wants to stop us helping Ukraine – but their actions will only lead us to do more for Ukraine. Russia’s actions are a sign of weakness, and a symptom of Putin’s failure in Ukraine.
To stay transatlantic, Nato is becoming more European. A Nato with Europe, and Canada, spending more, producing more, and doing more for their security. This is the idea of Nato 3.0.
Building for the future. A stronger Europe, in a stronger Nato.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK politics: Burnham says budget will be ‘challenging’ and denies he is just ‘tax and spend socialist’ – as it happened

articles.author: Jessica Elgot and Pippa Crerar
articles.description:
Labour has also increased fundraising from members in response to Reform’s £72m donations from crypto billionaires
Labour has hosted major party donors at No 10 for a drinks reception, as the party comes under growing pressure from MPs and unions to consider a donations cap.
The Guardian understands that high-level donors, including business leaders and philanthropists, were hosted by cabinet ministers in Downing Street for an evening reception on Tuesday. Donors from the party’s Rose Network give thousands of pounds a year to the party.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Labour holds No 10 drinks party for donors amid growing calls for donations cap

articles.author: Richard Partington Senior economics correspondent
articles.description:
PM rejects claim he leads a ‘tax-and-spend’ government, as Bank of England prepares for interest rates decision
Andy Burnham has said “difficult decisions” will need to be taken in next month’s budget after a rise in energy prices triggered by the Iran war drove UK inflation above 3%.
In a fresh blow for living standards amid the worsening damage to the global economy from the Middle East conflict, official figures showed soaring fuel prices pushed inflation from 2.9% in July to 3.1% in August.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham warns of ‘difficult decisions’ in budget as inflation rises to 3.1%

articles.author: Ben Quinn and Amelia Gentleman
articles.description:
Politicians from Solihull, Gateshead and Kent were in online group linked to balaclava-clad far-right agitators
At least five Reform UK councillors have been members of a Facebook group linked to the far-right group involved in the blockades of Dover and Portsmouth by masked men, according to anti-fascist campaigners.
Nigel Farage’s party has been wrestling with internal divisions over its position on the Patriot Platform group, whose activities have been condemned by Farage and across the political spectrum.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: At least five Reform councillors joined Facebook group linked to far-right Patriot Platform

articles.author: Dalya Alberge
articles.description:
Exclusive: Exhibition focusing on Finnish writer and artist’s illustrations will include original art from her first Moomins book
The Moomin books about lovable trolls with hippopotamus snouts who live in harmony with nature are a global publishing phenomenon, having sold up to 30m copies since the Finnish artist and writer Tove Jansson wrote and illustrated them between 1945 and 1977.
Now previously unseen drawings of her eccentric characters will be among more than 100 exhibits in a major exhibition that is being staged in London 25 years after her death.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Previously unseen drawings by Moomins author Tove Jansson to go on show in London

articles.author: Samuel Gibbs Consumer technology editor
articles.description:
Doorbell firm aims to replace WhatsApp or Facebook groups with platform where people can post about safety or lost pets
Amazon’s doorbell camera maker Ring is to launch its Neighbours community app in the UK in an attempt to supplant neighbourhood WhatsApp or Facebook groups.
The service is intended as a modern equivalent of a community message board, where neighbours can post about safety, community matters or lost pets.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Amazon to launch Ring ‘neighbourhood watch’ app in UK amid US privacy fears

articles.author: Ella Creamer
articles.description:
The British-American novelist and playwright who regularly appeared on current affairs shows will be remembered for her ‘warmth, humour and generosity’, says her husband
The British-American novelist, playwright and commentator Bonnie Greer has died aged 77.
In a statement, her husband David Hutchins said that she died on Tuesday evening following a brief illness.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bonnie Greer, writer and cultural commentator, dies aged 77

articles.author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
articles.description:
Exclusive: Plastic surfaces form hotspots with an increase of antibiotic-resistant genes, study finds
Microplastics act like a “Trojan horse” delivering pollutants, pesticides and bacteria through the soil, a five-year multinational research project has found.
The EU-funded project, which has so far resulted in 22 peer-reviewed studies, found microplastics in the soil of all 227 agricultural fields it tested across 11 European countries. The researchers said this poses a global threat, with healthy soils essential for life on Earth.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Microplastics in soil pose global threat by acting like ‘Trojan horse’ to deliver toxins

articles.author: Mark Sweney
articles.description:
Reach, which also owns Express, makes decision because of ‘mammoth shift’ in how audiences seek out content
The publisher of the Mirror and Express newspapers is to cut a further 220 editorial jobs as it adapts to a dramatic fall in online traffic while readers increasingly turn to summaries generated by artificial intelligence.
Reach, which also owns scores of online brands and regional titles including the Manchester Evening News, the Birmingham Mail and the Liverpool Echo, said the latest cuts were necessary to cope with a “mammoth shift” in how audiences seek out content.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mirror publisher to cut 220 editorial jobs as readers turn to AI summaries

articles.author: Alex Daniel
articles.description:
Latest attempt to secure future of Britain’s biggest car factory may be subject to UK weakening EV sales mandate
Nissan has said it will invest £170m to build a new SUV at its factory in Sunderland – but said the move was subject to the UK weakening its electric vehicle sales mandate.
The new hybrid model, the Kicks, is Nissan’s latest attempt to secure the future of the plant, which employs 6,000 people in Tyne and Wear and is Britain’s biggest car factory.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sunderland gets its Kicks: Nissan to invest £170m to build new hybrid SUV

articles.author: Lauren Almeida
articles.description:
Entain, which also owns Coral and BetMGM, starts consultation process over customer care roles

Business live – latest updates

The Ladbrokes owner, Entain, has said it is preparing to cut 400 jobs, only weeks after the FTSE 100 business reported better than expected profit in its first half of the year.
The gambling group, which also owns Coral and BetMGM, has started a consultation process that could remove one in five of its 2,000 customer care jobs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ladbrokes owner prepares to cut 400 jobs weeks after profit boost

articles.author: Matthew Pearce
articles.description:
New owners apply for permission to extract oil in Horse Hill despite landmark ruling from supreme court in 2024
After years of trying to dig for oil in Surrey, the company behind the drilling project that was turned down in a landmark supreme court ruling has sold off the site for a fraction of the money it spent on it, and rebranded as a clean energy company.
Meanwhile, the new owners, who picked up the site for £1m, are applying, once again, for permission to dig.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Company behind failed Surrey oilfield project sells site at massive loss

articles.author: Written by Tim Burrows and read by Sam Swainsbury. Produced by Nicola Alexandrou and Joshan Chana. The executive producer was Ellie Bury
articles.description:
We are raiding the Guardian long read archives to bring you some classic pieces from years past, with new introductions from the authors.
This week, from 2023: Landfill sites have swallowed many a beauty spot along the Thames estuary in the past 50 years. Now, as those dumps start to disgorge tonnes of mouldering detritus into the river, it truly feels like the Age of Consequences
By Tim Burrows. Read by Sam Swainsbury
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The rubbishscapes of Essex: why our buried trash is back to haunt us – podcast

articles.author: Anna Bawden Health and social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Analysis of 29 studies highlights potentially heightened danger from small particulate matter and nitrogen dioxide 
Air pollution is associated with an increased risk of suicide and suicidal thoughts, according to research.
Environmental pollution is known to be associated with poorer mental health but its role in suicide risk is less well understood. Scientists at Queen’s University Belfast examined whether air, noise, light, and water pollution could influence the risk of death by suicide and suicidal behaviours.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Air pollution linked to higher suicide risk, international research suggests

articles.author: David Conn
articles.description:
Decision not to pause proceedings means £18m report does not engage with concerns over former nurse’s conviction
Just two months before Lady Justice Kathryn Thirlwall opened her inquiry into events at the Countess of Chester hospital and the crimes of Lucy Letby, a report by Chris Henley KC was published into the “atrocious” wrongful conviction of Andrew Malkinson for rape.
Henley prefaced that report with a plea for the legal establishment to recognise that the criminal courts produce miscarriages of justice. Right up to top judges in the court of appeal, Henley wrote, the system has “a deep-seated … cultural reluctance” to accept it “will on occasion make mistakes” and that “entirely innocent defendants will sometimes be convicted”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thirlwall inquiry has left biggest questions around the Letby case unanswered

articles.description:
Bodycam footage released on 15 September shows former England footballer Raheem Sterling's arrest on 28 May, after he admitted to driving dangerously on the motorway. Sterling pleaded guilty at Basingstoke magistrates court on Tuesday to driving a Lamborghini Urus dangerously on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road before he crashed. The 31-year-old admitted possession of six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation, a class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen


Raheem Sterling could face prison for reckless driving while using nitrous oxide

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bodycam footage shows Raheem Sterling's arrest for dangerous driving – video

articles.author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
articles.description:
Lady Justice Thirlwall’s report concludes three babies might have survived if hospital had acted on concerns about nurse
Ministers have promised sweeping changes to the NHS after a “devastating” official review concluded that three babies might have survived if hospital bosses and doctors had acted on concerns about the nurse Lucy Letby.
A public inquiry found a “complete failure” to protect babies on the neonatal unit at the Countess of Chester hospital in north-west England.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ministers vow sweeping NHS changes after ‘devastating’ report on Lucy Letby hospital

articles.author: Damien Gayle Environment correspondent
articles.description:
Green-run council also curbing ads for airlines, cruises, fossil fuels and SUVs on its billboards and bus shelters
Bristol has become the first British city to impose a ban on the advertising of fast fashion, in new restrictions that will also curb ads for SUVs and airlines.
The ban is part of moves by the West Country city, known for its radical political scene, to impose sweeping bans on advertising for polluting industries.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bristol becomes first British city to ban advertisements for fast fashion

articles.author: Ben Beaumont-Thomas
articles.description:
Musician clarified her own health status after concerns were raised by interview with husband and bandmate Stephen Morris earlier this month
Gillian Gilbert, keyboardist with New Order, has announced she is again having treatment for cancer.
The 65-year-old musician announced the news on Instagram, as a response to an interview her husband and New Order bandmate, drummer Stephen Morris, gave to Rolling Stone earlier this month. Morris had said: “I’ve got a bit of a health problem at the minute, which precludes leaving the country for any length of time … it’s pretty serious.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: New Order keyboardist Gillian Gilbert announces she is ‘living with cancer’

articles.author: Robert Booth UK technology editor
articles.description:
Experts air concern over AI lingo redolent of James Joyce’s prose that is creating barriers to monitoring and oversight
AI models have begun communicating in a strange new version of English that reads like a cross between James Joyce’s Finnegans Wake and tech bro jargon, new research has found.
Autonomous AI agents are rapidly creating novel dialects allowing them to converse in an often barely comprehensible language, which risks making it harder for humans to monitor their behaviour.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: AI models chatting in ‘surreal’ dialect mixing poetic language and tech bro jargon

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Actor, who made history at the Emmys, thanked the ‘great and the good people of Wales’ for nurturing his talent
When Matthew Rhys made history as the first actor ever to win two best lead Emmy awards in one night, he paid tribute to his roots.
“To the great and good people of Wales, who were as much a nurturer as anyone else,” said the proud Welshman now living in New York, “We are a small but mighty nation”. “Diolch yn fawr iawn,” he added, meaning “thank you very much” in Welsh.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Matthew Rhys’s alma mater pays tribute to ‘loyal pupil’ and Welsh language devotee

articles.author: Jamie Grierson
articles.description:
Lady Justice Thirlwall’s wide-ranging inquiry calls on NHS England to implement 14 changes by March next year

Lady Justice Thirlwall has published the report on the findings of her inquiry into events at the Countess of Chester hospital involving the actions of former neonatal nurse Lucy Letby, who was convicted over the murder and attempted murder of multiple babies.
Here we take a look at the report and its findings.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thirlwall report: what did it say about Lucy Letby case and what does it recommend?

articles.author: Alex Daniel
articles.description:
Labour should replace levy in 2027 rather than 2030 as energy bills are poised to surge over the winter, says lobby group
The North Sea oil and gas industry has called on Labour to scrap the windfall tax on fossil fuel firms three years early, as Britain heads into a winter with energy bills expected to reach their highest level since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.
Offshore Energies UK (OEUK), the industry’s trade body, wants the tax replaced in 2027, rather than in 2030, with a narrower levy that only applies during price spikes.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Scrap windfall tax on oil and gas firms early, North Sea industry urges

articles.author: Sandra Laville
articles.description:
Grant applications in England surge as interest grows in habitat that captures carbon and helps reduce flood risk
The ancient craft of hedge laying is experiencing a strong revival as farmers use techniques that peaked in the 18th and 19th centuries to boost wildlife, capture carbon and help tackle flooding.
Hedge laying, which restores and revives mature hedges to keep them fresh, was among the four most popular categories of capital grants selected by farmers out of a total pot of £225m provided by the government this year to support practical environmental improvements on farms and across the countryside.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It’s really taking off’: hedge revival as farmers rediscover ancient tools

articles.author: Kiran Stacey and Henry Dyer
articles.description:
Key questions surrounding the huge sums donated by crypto billionaires Christopher Harborne and Ben Delo
Reform UK announced over the weekend the two biggest single political donations in British history: £36m from the Thailand-based crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne and a further £36m from another crypto billionaire, Ben Delo.
However, by Monday experts were questioning whether the donations would be legal, especially under the elections bill that the government is bringing through parliament and which will apply retrospectively.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Will the £72m of donations to Reform UK be allowed?

articles.author: Presented by Pippa Crerar and Kiran Stacey, produced by Nada Smiljanic, music by Axel Kacoutié; the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj
articles.description:
There’s been a huge backlash against Reform UK after the party received £72m from two crypto billionaires over the weekend.
Paul Nowak, the TUC leader, said the money showed democracy was ‘in crisis’. Labour is pushing for tighter restrictions on political donations which could be retrospective, but Reform is confident this will not affect its new war chest.
How much does this money change the political landscape? And with Labour receiving millions from unions, will its new rules backfire?
Please keep sending your comments and questions to politicsweeklyuk@theguardian.com.
Please follow and subscribe to the Politics Weekly YouTube channel here
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Party for sale’? Reform’s £72m donation causes backlash – podcast

articles.author: David Conn Investigations correspondent
articles.description:
Three years of research has uncovered 13,000 people who invested in Britain’s trafficking of enslaved Africans
The Register of British Slave Traders is the product of three years of research by a team of historians into all known investors in Britain’s near 250 years of trafficking enslaved African people, from the 16th to 19th centuries.
It provides profiles and biographical details of thousands of people who financed the British slave trade, which violently trafficked approximately 3 million African men, women and children across the Atlantic.
The Company of Royal Adventurers into Africa, founded in 1660;
The Company of Royal Adventurers Trading to Africa, founded in 1663;
The Royal African Company, founded 1672, which trafficked about 150,000 enslaved African people.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What is the Register of British Slave Traders and whom does it identify?

articles.description:
Several hundred anti-immigration protesters faced off with counter-protesters in the centre of Portsmouth on Saturday, as the southern English port city found itself at the heart of Britain’s increasingly acrimonious immigration debate. Under a heavy police presence, approximately 400 protesters marched into the centre of town for a second weekend, chanting slogans hostile to migrants. A similar number of people belonging to anti-racism groups joined them on the opposite side of the city’s Guildhall Square

Portsmouth experiences second weekend of anti-immigration protests
